content_text_body:
Social capital is the value that a team has, above and beyond the combined value of each individual member of a team. Social capital emerges when teams become supportive social networks. These strong networks allow us to accomplish what we can't on our own, whether it's completing a project on time, overcoming obstacles, or managing workplace stress. And when we help each other succeed, we experience greater meaning and well-being.

Consider these two ways to increase social capital:

### Be authentic

Team members cannot connect fully and support each other if they do not really know each other. Speak openly and honestly. Share ideas, concerns and plans. Encourage each other to be authentic by being yourself and accepting team members as they are.

### Support each other

Help each other overcome obstacles. Be an ally to your team members. For example, if you notice that someone on your team is not getting credit for an idea, reiterate whose idea it was. Or if you notice that someone is frazzled over a looming deadline, offer to bring them lunch.
